subject: Re: Follow-up: Model evals + multilingual QA - Globex Retail
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
To: Alice Park <alice.park@globexretail.com>, Tom Sato <tom.sato@globexretail.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.inference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2026-02-24T10:15:00-08:00
Subject: Follow-up: Model evals + multilingual QA - Globex Retail

Hi Alice / Tom —

Great speaking with you this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

1) Goals & constraints
- Primary use case: multi-lingual customer service summarization and intent classification (EN, FR, DE, NL, JA, KO).
- Quality bar: >90% intent accuracy for EU languages, >85% for APAC (initial target).
- Latency requirement: P95 < 300ms for short responses; batch/throughput considerations for nightly processing.

2) Recommended evaluation plan
- Short-term: run a focused eval on our LLM candidates (Redwood-3b-int8, Red-7b-qat, Red-13b-pt) with your sample prompt sets across locales.
- Metrics: intent accuracy, summary ROUGE/L, hallucination spot-checks, latency and token cost.
- We'll provide the prompt set + benchmark harness and upload initial results into a shared Drive folder.

3) Next steps / timeline
- Action: Globex to share 2k labeled examples (if possible) or a representative sample per locale by EOD next week (Mar 3).
- Action: Redwood to run baseline evals and return a summary + per-locale recommendations within 5 business days after receiving data.
- Option: If you want to also test private deployment for data residency in EU, we can include Redwood Private timeline separately.

Attachments: I’m attaching the initial prompt set we discussed (GLOBEX_eval_prompt_set_v1.jsonl) and a draft SOW so procurement has context.

Callouts / risks:
- Model regression risk: if we recommend a quantized 7b variant to lower cost, we should run strict quality regression tests on EU languages — some quantization paths can degrade morphological handling in German/Dutch.
- Tokenization mismatch: Japanese/Korean may need locale-specific tokenizer tweaks; we’ll surface that in the report.

Please confirm the data share timeline and whether procurement needs an initial SOW for review. Happy to jump on a short follow-up call.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

--
Attachment: GLOBEX_eval_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (1.2 MB - prompt set stub)
Attachment: SOW_draft_Globex.docx (docx stub)

From: Alice Park <alice.park@globexretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Tom Sato <tom.sato@globexretail.com>, Globex Procurement <procurement@globexretail.com>
Date: 2026-02-24T13:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Model evals + multilingual QA - Globex Retail

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Data share: We can provide ~1,500 labeled examples across EN/FR/DE/JA by next Wednesday (Mar 3). We’ll prioritize customer support tickets and agent summaries.
- SLA / residency: For EU deployment we’ll need data residency controls and SOC 2 evidence; procurement will review the SOW and loop in security.
- Cost sensitivity: Our ops team prefers a 7b-ish model if the quality delta vs 13b is acceptable — but accuracy in DE/NL is a hard requirement.

Quick ask: when you run the baselines, can you include a per-locale confusion matrix and a small qualitative sample for hallucination checks? That will help our product folks decide.

Tom and I are available Thurs 10–12 PT for a short follow-up if that helps.

Best,
Alice
Head of Customer Experience | Globex Retail
alice.park@globexretail.com

Date: 2026-02-25T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Model evals + multilingual QA - Globex Retail

Hi Alice / Tom —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the timeframe — that works. Per your asks, we’ll include: 
- Per-locale confusion matrices + top-5 error buckets
- A qualitative hallucination sample (10 examples per locale) with short notes on root causes
- Tokenization/encoding notes for JA/KO and any recommended tokenizer overrides

I’ve kicked off the baseline run with our evaluation team. Preliminary plan: run Redwood-3b-int8, Red-7b-qat (quantized-aware tuned), and Red-13b-pt (base). We’ll test each on your sample set once received.

Attached is the EU/APAC benchmark summary template we’ll use — we’ll populate the CSV and put a link into the Drive folder. Also attaching an initial SOW draft for procurement to review; happy to take redlines.

Proposed timeline:
- You send sample data by Mar 3.
- Redwood runs baselines Mar 4–6 and shares results + recommendation by EOD Mar 9.
- Optional canary: if you want to test private deployment or dedicated capacity for EU data residency, we can scope in parallel — feels like a 3–4 week project after contract.

Next step: Marissa — would you like me to schedule the Thurs 10am PT slot with Tom and Alice to confirm data share format?

Thanks,
Marissa

--

Subject: Internal: Globex evals - immediate next steps

Internal note — bringing you both up to speed. Summary of the external thread: Globex will send ~1.5k labeled examples across EN/FR/DE/JA by Mar 3. They want per-locale confusion matrices and hallucination samples. They are cost-sensitive and lean toward a 7b solution if quality holds for DE/NL.

Immediate asks for evaluation team (please):
- Nikhil: run Redwood-3b-int8, Red-7b-qat, Red-13b-pt on the sample once we ingest. Produce per-locale confusion matrices + top error buckets. Note any tokenization issues with JA/KO.
- Vivek: include inference latency and cost-per-1k-tokens estimates for each model/quant profile and a suggested quantization profile that minimizes DE/NL degradation.
- Timeline: ingest by Mar 3, run Mar 4–6, initial writeup by Mar 9.

I’ve attached the prompt set and CSV template we sent the customer. I’ll schedule a quick sync Thurs 10am PT to lock the data format.

Marissa
